solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Take recipe from doctor on ship: it's easily done

indicators.note: take, with 'from', tells us to remove one piece from another piece here

parts.note: Dr is the usual short title for a doctor
R is the abbreviation for recipe, the Latin 'take' heading a prescription
o' is a clipped form of 'on', as in 'cat-o'-nine-tails'
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A doctor at sea dispensing a remedy that requires no effort at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' looks like part of the prescription, but with 'from' it is the removal signal. 'Recipe' as R is a pun in itself: Latin for 'take'.
explanation.definitionFit: A doss is British slang for a task requiring little effort, something simple to get done.

clue.text: Life has a new start when one becomes this

definitions.text: Life has a new start when one becomes this

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word life is swapped for a different one here

explanation.surface: A newly married woman finds her existence begins afresh.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: change the opening L of LIFE to W, and marriage is the new start the clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who marries begins a new married existence as a spouse, the role the clue points at.

clue.text: Body parts found under Pelion?

definitions.meaning: Latin plural for bones, the framework parts of a body
in Greek myth the giants piled Mount Pelion on top of this other Thessalian mountain to reach heaven

explanation.surface: Anatomy discovered beneath a Greek mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'to pile Pelion on Ossa' (add difficulty to difficulty) comes from the giants' attempt to storm Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: Bones are parts of the body, and Ossa is the Latin plural for them; the mountain sits beneath Pelion in the myth.

clue.text: Airs moving at several knots or one knot

parts.note: moving air at a measurable speed is wind, and several such are winds
taken as written

explanation.surface: Breezes measured in nautical speed, alongside a single tied knot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knots' first means a speed at sea, then a tie knot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Windsor is a wide triangular necktie knot, so it is an example of a knot.

clue.text: Depressed stomach in Balmoral, perhaps

parts.note: feeling blue means being low in spirits
the bonnet is another name for the reticulum, the second stomach of a cow or other ruminant

explanation.surface: A queasy, gloomy feeling at the royal Scottish castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral is the royal estate in Scotland, but here it is a flat Scottish cap; 'stomach' is a ruminant's second stomach, not a human belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A balmoral is a flat woollen Scottish cap, one kind of the broad blue cap worn by Scots.

clue.text: Ruler who lost his head to issue oil in chaos at the borders of Zimbabwe

indicators.note: being in chaos means jumbled up, so the letters of issue oil get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A deposed ruler sending out oil in disorder along an African country's frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ISSUE OIL gives LOUISSEI, then ZE comes from the edges of Zimbabwe.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis XVI of France (French 'seize' = sixteen) was guillotined in 1793, a king beheaded.

clue.text: Able to raise tax on gold in European currency rarely

indicators.note: in places the tax and gold pieces inside the currency word

parts.note: ley is a rare form of leu, the currency of Romania and Moldova
VAT is value added tax
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A financial proposal about taxing bullion held in a continental currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just joins VAT and OR in order. LEY is a rare spelling of the Romanian leu, hence 'rarely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elevatory serves to lift or raise, like a muscle that lifts a part of the body.

clue.text: Sounds like a jump round which everything revolves

indicators.note: says the word for the jump is heard, not written

parts.note: an axel is a figure-skating jump

explanation.surface: A leap pivoted at the centre of all movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The axel is a figure-skating jump named after Axel Paulsen.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel turns on the central rod or spindle, so it is what everything revolves round.

clue.text: Car squashed a mole outside Portuguese city

indicators.note: outside puts the jumbled letters around the city name
squashed means crushed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Faro is a city on the Algarve in southern Portugal

explanation.surface: A vehicle ran over a small burrowing animal near a Portuguese town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squashed' turns A MOLE into ALMEO, which goes outside FARO: AL + FARO + MEO.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfa Romeo is an Italian motor manufacturer, so its name stands for a make of motor vehicle.

clue.text: Speedy flight with wingless insect up

indicators.note: with here means holding, so one piece is carried inside the other

parts.note: a rider who is up is in the saddle
a ked is a wingless fly that lives on sheep

explanation.surface: A rapid escape accompanied by a flightless bug rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' is not a reversal: a jockey who is 'up' is in the SADDLE, which holds KED.
explanation.definitionFit: To skedaddle is to run off hurriedly, a quick getaway.

clue.text: Dandy almost dishonoured

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a dude is a fop or dandy

explanation.surface: A dapper fellow nearly disgraced.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque the bank refuses to pay is a worthless one, so a bounced cheque is a useless dud.

clue.text: Following bird that's loose

parts.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a ree is a female ruff, a wading bird

explanation.surface: Chasing a bird that has escaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something loose is unconfined or at liberty, not tied up.

clue.text: Six advanced by way of road

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
A stands for advanced, as in A-level

explanation.surface: Half a dozen moved forward along a highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By way of' is itself a sense of the answer, but 'road' (Latin, as in the Appian Way) is the definition; 'by way of' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin and in Roman place names the word means a road or highway, as in the Via Appia.

clue.text: Wife who was murdered (goddess consuming evil spirits tail first)

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the goddess word encloses the other piece

parts.note: dea is Latin for a goddess

indicators.note: tail first means the final letter is brought round to the front

parts.note: demons are evil spirits

explanation.surface: A murdered woman, described as a deity devouring devils backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tail first' is a cyclic shift, not a reversal: only the last letter jumps to the front. DEA is Latin, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello's wife in Shakespeare's tragedy is smothered by her jealous husband.

clue.text: Made play with dames: Triad cut up rough

indicators.note: to cut up rough is to turn violent, so the letters are knocked about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Elderly ladies joked about with a Chinese gang turned nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made play with' suggests teasing, but 'Made play' is the definition and 'with' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To dramatise is to turn a story into a stage or screen drama.

clue.text: More than one table held cue broken in extremes of stress

indicators.note: in puts the jumbled letters inside the outer pair
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
broken means smashed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A snooker player's cue snaps under pressure while he's holding it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Table' suggests snooker in the surface, but it means a list or timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule is a timetable or list, so several of them are tables.

clue.text: Awakening memories of octave I've lost

indicators.note: lost means astray or out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the apostrophe is ignored, so the contraction gives its letters unchanged

explanation.surface: A musician lamenting a missing octave in a nostalgic piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost' looks like part of the musician's lament, but it is the signal to rearrange; the contraction then follows unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evocative calls up feelings or recollections of the past.

clue.text: In shelter demonstration fails to start

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a proof is a demonstration of truth

explanation.surface: A protest inside a refuge doesn't get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demonstration' suggests a protest; here it is a proof.
explanation.definitionFit: The top covering of a building gives cover, so it is a shelter.

clue.text: Condition is reversed about dust on forge

indicators.note: about means going round the dust word
reversed means the condition word is read backwards

parts.note: if introduces a condition
ash is the dust left by a fire
taken as written

explanation.surface: A smith's work state turned around by dust on the anvil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' is a link. IF reversed gives FI, which goes about ASH, then ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To fashion something is to shape or make it, as a smith does when he forges metal.

clue.text: Food for public parks

definitions.meaning: shared provisions or rations, as at a college
open land for the use of all, like the London greens

explanation.surface: Provisions for town green spaces.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both shared rations and areas of public open land.

clue.text: Transfer without a penny for City

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the penny is removed

parts.note: a handover is a transfer of control
d is the old British abbreviation for a penny, from Latin denarius

explanation.surface: A transfer completed with no money paid, involving a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanover is a major city in northern Germany, capital of Lower Saxony.

clue.text: One who's crazy about skate …

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the crazy word goes round the one

parts.note: mad means crazy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone who is passionate about ice skating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skate' is not the sport but the fish: a young skate or ray.
explanation.definitionFit: A young skate or thornback ray is called by this name, so a skate fits as an example.

clue.text: … can stay to play regardless of consequences

indicators.note: to play with the letters is to move them around freely

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone may remain to perform whatever the outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to the previous clue; it has no wordplay role.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something whatever the price means doing it without regard to the results.

clue.text: Boat for jazz fan

definitions.meaning: a catboat is a single-masted sailing vessel, often shortened
in jazz slang a hip enthusiast or player is a cool ...

explanation.surface: A vessel for a lover of swing music.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small sailing boat and, in slang, a jazz enthusiast.

clue.text: Finally you fell somewhat short last month

indicators.note: finally picks out the end letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: In the end you were a bit lacking in the previous month.
explanation.walkthrough: Ult. abbreviates Latin 'ultimo', last month, used in old business letters; 'short' marks the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation of ultimo, meaning in the previous month, as in 'your letter of the 5th ult.'

clue.text: Damon, perhaps, in car without attendant

indicators.note: without means minus, so the attendant word is taken away

parts.note: the Hillman was a British car make, such as the Hillman Imp
a man is a manservant or attendant

explanation.surface: A racing driver sitting in his car with no helper.
explanation.walkthrough: Damon Hill was the 1996 Formula One world champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Damon Hill is an example of someone bearing that surname, a British racing driver.

clue.text: Club's high quality hard white earthenware …

parts.note: an iron is a golf club, and the 's gives the S
tone means class or high quality, as in raising the tone

explanation.surface: A golf club's prestige compared to fine pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironstone china is a hard, durable white pottery first made in Staffordshire.

clue.text: Leo's cross

definitions.meaning: Leo is one of the twelve zodiac constellations
an X made by someone who cannot write serves as a signature

explanation.surface: A man named Leo is angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leo's' reads as 'Leo is'; 'cross' looks like 'angry' but is a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is a zodiac sign, and a cross is a mark made in place of a signature.

clue.text: Nothing to write with in clear space

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
a pen is something to write with

explanation.surface: No writing instrument in an empty area.
explanation.definitionFit: An open space is an unobstructed, clear area.

clue.text: Domestic servant's regularly messenger

indicators.note: regularly picks out every other letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A household servant who regularly carries messages.
explanation.walkthrough: Esne is an Anglo-Saxon labourer or servant, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: An esne was a household slave or hired labourer in Anglo-Saxon England.

clue.text: …where one eats pie

definitions.meaning: a dining hall for officers or servicemen
printers' pie is jumbled type, a muddle

explanation.surface: The place someone eats a pastry dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pie' is printers' pie, type spilled into disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a military dining room and a muddle, as pie does in printing.

clue.text: Place for putting in "English Poetry" endlessly popular pieces

indicators.note: in places the golfing piece inside the other letters
endlessly means its final letter is cut off

parts.note: verse is poetry
on a golf course, putting is done on the green

explanation.surface: A golfer reading English poetry on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting' is the golf stroke, not placing. GREEN goes inside E + VERS(E).
explanation.definitionFit: Evergreens are songs or tunes that stay popular for years.
